operations.contract: Read a root or selected struct object from a stream, span, or read-only memory region.
Read values and exact source byte ranges.
Resolve a root, field, array element, or pointer target without changing the caller's position.
Return a fixed/runtime array count or terminated-string character count.
Serialize a root or selected value to an owned array, caller-owned span, or IBufferWriter<byte>.
Write a root or selected value at the caller's current position.
Locate and replace an existing root or selected value while restoring the caller's position.
Read a natural scalar or composite value from a stream or memory region, optionally mapping it to a checked CLR type.

statuses.verified: Supported and backed by executable evidence for this operation.
statuses.limited: Supported only under the row's documented limitations and backed by executable evidence.
statuses.notApplicable: The operation has no meaningful contract for this feature row.
statuses.blocked: The intended contract requires an unresolved decision or planned implementation.

variableInputContract.snapshot: Caller entries are copied into isolated mutable operation state and are never modified.
variableInputContract.precedence: Caller entries override matching layout #define names.
variableInputContract.compatibility: The greenfield public API exposes one read-only integer shape; parser expression nodes remain internal.

memoryIoContract.lifetime: Every memory operation is synchronous and retains no caller buffer after returning.
memoryIoContract.pointerCoordinates: Pointer positions are zero-based within the supplied input region or newly serialized output region, including sliced memory and appends to an existing writer.
memoryIoContract.partialFailure: Span output can leave an initialized prefix changed, and IBufferWriter output can retain advanced windows, when a later write fails; neither caller-owned destination promises rollback.
memoryIoContract.webIntegration: Browser contract v4 accepts Uint8Array input and Base64 output through the shared parse/serialize/update bridge; bridge copying is measured separately from the zero-adapter managed memory APIs.

compiledExecutionContract.structTraversal: Every non-union read route executes declaration-order fields through one compiled struct executor and consumes the actual runtime extent plus compiled tail alignment.
compiledExecutionContract.unionTraversal: Every union read route uses one overlapping-member executor; a struct member begins at the union address but its own child fields advance sequentially.
compiledExecutionContract.debug: Debug capture observes the same compiled read and does not interpret a second field loop.

operationContextContract.snapshotBoundary: Read, write, and update settings are copied before variable enumeration, payload access, stream access, or another caller-controlled callback.
operationContextContract.readState: One CStructOperationContext owns resolved variables, the physical-read budget stream, addressing policy, structure and pointer depth, pointer-cycle tracking, bitfield progress, and optional debug diagnostics.
operationContextContract.selectedState: Target location and selected-target consumption reuse the same context and cannot reset byte, array, structure, pointer, string, or cycle accounting.
operationContextContract.cycleKey: Active pointer targets use value-tuple keys of address, compiled type name, and remaining pointer depth without allocating composite strings.

managedApiCompatibilityContract.browserIntegration: Paired with the independent frozen browser-rc1 contract v4 baseline and validator; managed and browser changes remain reviewed independently.

roundTripStatuses.verified: Continuously proved for every value inside the listed supported domain.
roundTripStatuses.conditional: Continuously proved only under the listed normalization, representation, or caller-context conditions.
roundTripStatuses.blocked: No safe promise is made until the listed work item or design decision is complete.
roundTripStatuses.notApplicable: The feature describes a failure rather than a serializable value representation.

conditions: The caller supplies a CLR value representable by the declared primitive codec.
The same layout byte order and explicit endian override are used for parsing and serialization.
Fixed character buffers normalize a shorter input string to the declared width by appending NUL characters.
Bytes are exact after the first canonical serialization, including the declared-width NUL padding.
Text is valid for the selected encoding and does not contain that codec's terminator.
The input is the canonical encoding of valid text followed by exactly one complete codec terminator.
The declaration resolves to a signed or unsigned 8/16/32/64-bit integral backing domain and supplied writes are exact in-domain integers or declared symbolic names.
Known and unknown payloads use the complete declared signed/unsigned backing domain and the layout instance byte order.
Declared unsigned slices obey ADR-010's portable semantics and each supplied value fits its declared width.
Every bit in the storage unit is represented by declared portable slices; unnamed and zero-width forms remain excluded.
The supplied collection has exactly the declared zero, one, or multiple element shape.
Every element representation has its own applicable exact-byte contract.
Parsing and serialization receive the same layout-variable bindings and the supplied collection matches the evaluated count.
The same variables produce the same element count and every element representation has its own applicable exact-byte contract.
Every nested member representation has its own applicable value contract.
Every nested member is byte-stable and any aligned padding is already canonical.
Every inline member representation has its own applicable value contract.
Every inline member is byte-stable and any aligned padding is already canonical.
The resolved underlying representation has its own applicable value contract.
The resolved underlying representation has its own applicable byte contract.

An untagged parse returns complete raw storage and decoded member views with no selected member; a new or edited write must explicitly select one member, and parsing the resulting bytes returns to the neutral unselected representation.

An unchanged parsed or FromRaw union writes its complete extent exactly; explicit selected-member serialization produces canonical zero-filled storage, while whole-union updates follow the documented clear/preserve policy.
The stored address and optional dereferenced view are parsed, but root serialization writes the pointer address rather than relocating or serializing the target graph.
Exact-byte round-trip applies to pointer storage inside the selected root extent; external target bytes are outside that serialization.
Every parsed pointer level preserves its stored address, but root serialization writes only the top-level pointer storage.
Exact-byte round-trip applies only to pointer storage inside the selected root extent, not the external pointer chain or final target.
Parsing and serialization use the same aligned mode, layout byte order, and explicit field overrides.
New serialization canonicalizes alignment gaps and tail padding to zero; arbitrary source padding bytes are not represented by the value model and are not promised to survive.
A bounded failure has no successfully materialized value to round-trip.
Read failure behavior is covered by safety and atomicity contracts rather than serialization equivalence.
An invalid layout is rejected before a value representation exists.
An invalid layout has no supported byte representation.

knownContractLimits.summary: Root ParseStream returns the selected struct, while root ParseStreamWithDebug retains the declaration-name wrapper used by the legacy debug API.
Debug parsing records pointer storage and fields inside composite targets, but not the final primitive target range of a pointer or multi-pointer chain.

features.title: Fixed-width integer and character scalars
limitations: Portable aliases have repository-defined widths; they do not infer the host C ABI.

features.title: Narrow and UTF-16 character scalars and fixed buffers
limitations: char is one byte and wchar is one UTF-16 code unit; neither width follows the host platform.

features.title: Strict ASCII, UTF-8, and UTF-16 terminated strings
limitations: In-place replacement is non-extending and does not resize or relocate following layout fields; variable-length replacement must fit the caller's existing storage plan.

features.title: Named enums with explicit primitive backing
Portable unsigned bit slices in integral storage
limitations: Unnamed, zero-width, array, typedef-backed, enum-backed, and compiler-profile bitfield forms are deliberately rejected.

features.title: Zero-, one-, and many-element fixed arrays
limitations: Only one array dimension is represented; repeated C dimensions remain unsupported.

features.title: One-dimensional arrays sized by bounded expressions or caller variables
limitations: Counts use bounded checked signed Int32 expressions and one-dimensional collection shape.

features.title: Lexically scoped inline structs
limitations: Anonymous inline type identities are not exported names and cannot be referenced from unrelated fields.

features.title: Primitive, composite, array, and pointer typedef chains
limitations: The accepted grammar does not yet cover all common anonymous and tag-plus-alias C typedef forms.

features.title: Direct, relative, nullable, and typed data pointers
limitations: Dereference is policy/budget controlled, and serialization writes stored pointer addresses without relocating or emitting external target graphs.

Null encodes zero only for a scalar pointer value or selected pointer-array element; a null pointer collection and every null non-pointer/composite value fail with CStructWriteException across all supported binding shapes.
A parsed pointer is always an explicit Pointer result: address zero is null and never dereferenced, while a non-null pointer is either unresolved with no Value or dereferenced with its target.

features.title: Multi-level data-pointer chains
limitations: Pointer traversal is limited by explicit depth, target-range, nesting, and physical-read budgets.
Debug data records the pointer storage but does not yet add a range for a final primitive pointer target.

features.title: Natural alignment and field-level endian overrides
limitations: The portable natural-alignment policy is global; source-level pack/alignment directives and named compiler profiles are not yet supported.

features.title: Truncation, traversal budgets, and write budgets
Invalid syntax, names, types, recursion, and storage combinations

exclusions.syntax: struct Foo value; union U value; enum E value;
exclusions.rationale: The current ordinary-name grammar does not implement C tag namespaces.
exclusions.diagnosticPolicy: Reject during layout construction; never reinterpret the tokens as another supported declaration.

exclusions.syntax: typedef struct { ... } Name; and tag/alias variants
exclusions.rationale: Only the repository's narrower typedef forms are accepted today.
exclusions.diagnosticPolicy: Reject unsupported forms during layout construction.

exclusions.syntax: unsigned long long, signed char, uint32_t, and integer suffixes
exclusions.rationale: Portable explicit-width codecs exist, but the general C declaration spelling grammar does not.
exclusions.diagnosticPolicy: Require a documented repository spelling or reject construction.

exclusions.syntax: _Bool, bool, float, double, and long double
exclusions.rationale: No public value, endian, NaN, or ABI representation contract has been approved.
exclusions.diagnosticPolicy: Reject as an unknown field type during layout construction.

exclusions.rationale: The compiled model and public result shape currently represent one dimension.
exclusions.diagnosticPolicy: Reject repeated dimensions rather than silently flattening them.

exclusions.rationale: There is no implicit safe count or byte extent for a general flexible member.
exclusions.diagnosticPolicy: Reject until an explicit extent policy is supplied.

exclusions.rationale: The current data-pointer grammar cannot safely distinguish or invoke function pointers.
exclusions.diagnosticPolicy: Reject rather than treating the declaration as a data pointer.

exclusions.syntax: unnamed fields, zero-width separators, typedef/enum storage, and ABI-specific allocation
exclusions.rationale: The accepted portable subset requires named fields and direct built-in integral storage.
exclusions.diagnosticPolicy: Reject during layout compilation with a storage-capability diagnostic.

exclusions.syntax: includes, function macros, conditionals, token pasting, and stringification
exclusions.rationale: CStructSharp consumes standalone layout definitions and is not a general C preprocessor.
exclusions.diagnosticPolicy: Reject unsupported directives; a future header frontend must be an explicit separate boundary.

exclusions.syntax: int a, b; and mixed pointer/array declarators
exclusions.rationale: The current field grammar accepts one declarator per declaration.
exclusions.diagnosticPolicy: Reject the declaration rather than applying the first shape to every name.

exclusions.rationale: Accepted positions and whether layout-neutral qualifiers are preserved have not been decided.
exclusions.diagnosticPolicy: Reject instead of silently ignoring unrecognized tokens.

exclusions.syntax: anonymous struct/union members promoted into the containing path
exclusions.rationale: Inline declarations currently require a containing field name and do not promote members.

exclusions.syntax: #pragma pack, packed attributes, and explicit alignas/declspec alignment
exclusions.rationale: Only the constructor's portable aligned/unaligned policy is currently available.
exclusions.diagnosticPolicy: Reject unknown directives/attributes; never infer host packing.

exclusions.rationale: No compiler profile may be claimed without approved identity/version rules and differential fixtures.
exclusions.diagnosticPolicy: Use only the documented portable policy; never infer the host compiler or process ABI.
